  "limitations_stated": [
    "Some longstanding animal models have failed to result in therapeutic advances in the clinical setting.",
    "most models for diabetic nephropathy are unsatisfactory in that they do not evolve to renal failure.",
    "Satisfactory models for additional nephropathies are needed.",
    "Limitations of the model include the need for two surgical interventions, the second one having a high mortality rate, especially in mice, and requiring technical expertise.",
    "In addition, it is irreversible and the amount of kidney left to study is small and may be distorted by the surgical procedure.",
    "None of the many animal models perfectly replicate the human disease.",
    "However, since it is unilateral, no increased serum creatinine is observed, although the injured kidney develops all features of CKD: interstitial inﬂammation, tubular cell injury, and ﬁbrosis.",
    "However, the lack of the important component of bacterial proliferation in the LPS model led to the use of cecal-puncture and ligation, a more complex, less reproducible model, where bacteria are released into the peritoneum.",
    "No experimental treatment successfully tested in murine LPS models has demonstrated efﬁcacy in humans.",
    "Preeclampsia is thought to occur spontaneously only in women.",
    "Animal models of preeclampsia have obvious limitations.",
    "Mouse models are useful for genetic manipulation, but they are less useful for studying several key aspects of the pathogenesis of preeclampsia.",
    "These limitations also apply to many pharmacologically-induced models of preeclampsia.",
    "Furthermore, most models of preeclampsia do not include the complete spectrum of pathophysiological changes observed in humans.",
    "In most of these models, renal failure does not appear or it has not been assessed."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "Around 15% of patients suffering AKI progress to CKD",
    "Over 80% of patients with CKD have hypertension",
    "A progressive increase in albuminuria, progressive loss in renal function, severe glomerulosclerosis and interstitial ﬁbrosis, hypertension, cardiac ﬁbrosis, and anemia was observed by 4 weeks in CD-1 mice and by 12 weeks in 129S3 mice.",
    "After 16 weeks, the C57BL/6 mice had increased albuminuria without increased blood pressure and without developing progressive CKD or cardiac ﬁbrosis.",
    "In mice 0.3% adenine mixed with food for 10 days followed by 0.15–0.20% for maintenance has been recommended to avoid deaths.",
    "Later lowering adenine from 0.2% to 0.15% resulted in amelioration of renal function, although no formal reversibility studies were performed.",
    "In transgenic rats speciﬁcally expressing the human diphtheria toxin receptor in podocytes, diphtheria toxin dose-dependently caused podocyte depletion.",
    "Loss of up to 20% of podocytes caused transient proteinuria.",
    "A greater (21–40%) loss of podocytes caused focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with sustained mild proteinuria but normal renal function.",
    "Over 40% podocyte depletion caused full-blown focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, severe proteinuria and reduced renal function."
  ]
